title: II) Order of reaction: zeroth, first and second order graphs
summary: For A -> products, a 3x4 grid compares zeroth, first and second order reactions: their rate equations, concentration-time graphs, rate-concentration graphs and units of k. Zeroth order: [A] falls linearly and rate is constant (independent of [A]). First order: [A] decays exponentially and rate is directly proportional to [A] (slope = k). Second order: [A] decays faster at first then flattens, and rate vs [A] is a curve (rate vs [A]^2 is a straight line).

blocks.text: II) Order of reaction. For a reaction represented by: A -> products
Header row: Zeroth order | First order | Second order. Row 'Rate equation': Rate = k | Rate = k[A] | Rate = k[A]^2

Concentration-time graphs ([A] vs Time): zeroth = straight line decreasing linearly to the time axis; first = curve decreasing steeply then flattening towards the axis; second = curve decreasing steeply (more sharply than first) then flattening

Rate-concentration graphs: zeroth = horizontal line, slope = 0, labelled k on the Rate axis; first = straight line through the origin, slope = k, x-axis [A]; second = upward-curving line through the origin vs [A], and a straight line (slope = k) vs [A]^2; x-axis 'A or [A]^2'
Row 'Unit of rate constant, k': mol dm^-3 s^-1 (M s^-1) | s^-1 | mol^-1 dm^3 s^-1 (M^-1 s^-1)

Zeroth: 'y = c' (yellow); 'rate is only affected by value of k'; 'decrease linearly / stably'; 'rate is a constant'; 'up temp, up k, up rate !'; 'conc. of reactant doesn't affect rate!'. First: 'y = mx + c, c = 0'; 'decrease quickly'; 'steep'; 'decrease slowly'; 'flat'; 'near to 0'; 'up conc., up rate !'; 'C = 0' (circled origin); 'directly proportional'. Second: 'y = mx + c, c = 0 , if x is [A]^2'; 'decrease quickly'; 'steep'; 'decrease slowly'; 'flat, not near to 0'; 'up conc., up rate!'. Top-left: 'y = mx + c'.

key_concepts: Zeroth order: Rate = k; [A] decreases linearly; rate independent of [A]
First order: Rate = k[A]; exponential-type decay of [A]; rate directly proportional to [A]; rate-[A] slope = k
Second order: Rate = k[A]^2; rate-[A] is a curve, rate-[A]^2 is a straight line with slope = k
Concentration-time graph gradient magnitude = rate at that moment
Units of k: mol dm^-3 s^-1, s^-1, mol^-1 dm^3 s^-1
Increasing temperature increases k and therefore the rate

animation.concept: Order of reaction decides how the rate responds to falling [A]: the gradient of the concentration-time curve is the rate, and it stays constant (zeroth), falls in proportion to [A] (first) or falls with [A]^2 (second).
animation.why: The page is a static comparison grid. Running one moving cursor through all three concentration-time graphs while a live tangent and a rate bar update ties the two rows together (graph shape equals rate-concentration relationship). Page 4 builds a graph from data; this page is a side-by-side comparison with a live cursor, not a construction.

steps.visual: Three floating panels side by side titled Zeroth, First, Second, each with axes (x: Time, y: [A], no numbers). Each shows its curve fading in: zeroth = straight descending line from [A]0 (top-left) to the time axis; first = exponential decay [A] = [A]0 e^(-kt); second = [A] = [A]0/(1+k[A]0 t) hyperbolic decay. All three start at the same [A]0 and the same initial slope magnitude so the shapes can be compared.
steps.caption: Concentration-time graphs for A -> products

steps.visual: A white dot moves along each curve from t = 0 to the end, synchronised. At each dot, a short tangent line (yellow) is drawn. Below each panel, a horizontal bar 'Rate = gradient' shows the tangent steepness: zeroth bar stays full length for the whole run; first bar shrinks smoothly toward ~0; second bar shrinks faster at first then slowly.
steps.caption: Gradient of the curve = rate at that moment

steps.visual: Dot returns to t = 0. Zeroth panel: text 'Rate = k, constant'. First panel: text 'steep -> flat'. Second panel: text 'steep -> flat, but not as near 0'. Lower half of each panel switches to the rate vs concentration graph: Rate axis vertical, [A] axis horizontal. Zeroth: horizontal line at height k labelled 'slope = 0'.
steps.caption: Rate vs concentration: the same three reactions

steps.visual: First panel: straight line through origin appears, red circle at origin labelled 'C = 0', label 'slope = k', label 'directly proportional'. The moving dot's [A] value is projected as a vertical marker on this line and its height equals the rate bar.
steps.caption: First order: rate directly proportional to [A]

steps.visual: Second panel: curve through origin, curving upward, as rate vs [A]. Then x-axis relabels from [A] to [A]^2 and the curve straightens into a line through origin, 'slope = k'.
steps.caption: Second order: rate vs [A]^2 is a straight line

steps.visual: Units row appears under panels: 'mol dm^-3 s^-1', 's^-1', 'mol^-1 dm^3 s^-1'.
steps.caption: Unit of k depends on the order

correctness_notes: Zeroth-order [A]-t graph is a straight line: constant gradient equals constant rate = k
First-order [A]-t graph is an exponential decay that approaches zero but never reaches it (page notes 'flat, near to 0')
Second-order [A]-t graph also decays and flattens but more steeply at first and more slowly at the end (page notes 'flat, not near to 0'); never touches zero
Rate-[A] for zeroth order is a horizontal line (slope 0) at value k
Rate-[A] for first order is a straight line through the origin with slope = k (y = mx + c with c = 0)
Rate-[A] for second order is a parabola-shaped curve through origin; rate-[A]^2 is straight with slope = k
The page's concentration-time graphs have no numeric scales: use arbitrary units and do not display numbers on those axes
A real zeroth order curve would stop when [A] reaches 0; draw the line ending on the time axis
